description: US-36 The derived rules follow sessions, not the calendar. After US-34 and US-35, TWO THINGS STILL READ THE CALENDAR. FIRST, THE NO-SHOW COUNT: „how many of their own distributions has this household missed in a row" is counted by walking backwards through the calendar a fortnight at a time, asking the week anchor which colour each week carried — so EVERY CANCELLED WEEK IN THAT WALK IS COUNTED AS A MISS NOBODY MADE. It now counts SESSIONS THAT ACTUALLY TOOK PLACE: a session counts against a household when it has ENDED, its groups INCLUDE the household's group, it STARTED AFTER the household joined the register, and it holds NO HAND-OUT for them. The running session never counts. The figure stays DISPLAY ONLY — no threshold, no automatic archive — and a block is still deliberately NOT excluded. SECOND, THE SETTINGS SCREEN: it still holds a week anchor („KW 02/2026 war Rot") and a distribution weekday. After US-34 NOTHING reads the weekday at all and the anchor is read by exactly ONE line on the Start screen. BOTH ARE REMOVED WITHOUT REPLACEMENT — a settings value with no effect is one that eventually gets maintained wrongly, and a screen predicting „die nächste Ausgabe ist am Donnerstag (Rot)" makes a promise the software no longer has any way to keep. The software stops predicting when the next distribution is and what colour a week carries; it knows what happened and what is happening, and that is all it claims. WHAT GOES WITH THE ANCHOR is a satisfying amount of code: weekColour.ts's ISO-week arithmetic, distributionDay.ts, get-week-colour.ts, three SettingsVersion columns, two form controls, three variants of the SettingsChange union, the WeekColour/WeekAnchor/IsoWeekday types, and the BERLIN-DAY MATCHING of attended days in the no-show walk. WHAT STAYS is startOfUtcDay, which the certificate comparison needs and which MOVES to src/domain/calendarDay.ts — and berlinDayKey ITSELF, which this batch was written believing the walk was the last caller of: the 13-year boundary has read it since US-13.1 because a birthday turns over at Berlin midnight (householdComposition.ts), so it stays in attendance.ts with that one caller. A HOUSEHOLD'S GROUP IS UNCHANGED: still groupOf(customerNumber), even is BLUE and odd is RED (ADR-017), shown everywhere it is shown today — only the statement „this week is RED" disappears. ORDER WITHIN THE BATCH is inside-out for the rule half (1, 2) and OUTSIDE-IN for the removal half (3 domain, 4 schema, 5 screens): built the other way round, story 3 would break every caller at once. The EXHAUSTIVE SWITCH on SettingsChange is the safety net — the build fails until the settings screen stops rendering the three removed kinds. SCHEMA CHANGE: yes, three columns dropped, so prisma/migrations/ is REGENERATED and BOTH hand-written indexes (Customer.customerNumber partial unique, and the one-running-session index) MUST BE PUT BACK — story 4. THE FAILURE MODE OF A REMOVAL IS A SURVIVOR — a dictionary key, a comment, a test helper — which is why story 5 makes a grep an acceptance criterion, as US-27 did. NO NEW ADR: ADR-020 already recorded this removal as its own consequence. Requirements: local_only/manually-start-ausgabe/refined-requirements.md requirement D. Full PRD: tasks/prd-us-36-sessions-not-the-calendar.md

userStories.title: A no-show is a session that was missed (domain)
userStories.description: As DF, I want the no-show figure to count the afternoons that actually happened, so that the number beside a household means what I think it means. Source: tasks/prd-us-36-sessions-not-the-calendar.md §US-36.1
acceptanceCriteria: src/domain/distribution/noShows.ts is REWRITTEN around sessions. Its input becomes { sessions, attendedSessionIds, customerGroup, registeredOn } — NO settings, NO weekday, NO anchor, NO clock

A session counts against a household when ALL FOUR hold: it has ENDED; its groups INCLUDE the household's group; it STARTED AFTER the household joined the register; and it holds NO HAND-OUT for that household. THE RUNNING SESSION NEVER COUNTS

consecutiveNoShows walks the ended sessions NEWEST FIRST and stops at the first one the household collected at, or at their registration. 0 still means both „came last time" and „has not seen a session yet" — the same thing as far as archiving goes
A DISCARDED session is never in the input at all: the store filters it out, so the rule does not have to know the state exists

The module comment KEEPS the two things that stay true — the figure is DISPLAY ONLY, no threshold lives here and nothing automatic follows from any value; and a BLOCK IS DELIBERATELY NOT EXCLUDED. It DROPS the three calendar boundaries, which the four conditions replace, and it does NOT narrate that it used to count weeks

The BERLIN-DAY MATCHING of attended days leaves noShows.ts with the walk it served — attendance is matched by SESSION ID from here on, not by calendar day. berlinDayKey ITSELF STAYS in attendance.ts: the 13-year boundary has called it since US-13.1 and a birthday still turns over at Berlin midnight. Prove it: grep -rn berlinDayKey src/ tests/ leaves householdComposition.ts as the only caller

WRITTEN TEST-FIRST, one named test per rule: counts a session the household's group was served at and they missed / does not count a session that served only the other group / counts a session that served both groups / does not count the session that is still running / does not count a session that started before the household joined / stops counting at the last session they collected at / answers zero for a household that has not seen a session yet
Domain coverage stays at 100%
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: This story fixes a real bug: today every cancelled week in the walk is counted as a miss nobody made. Do not keep a calendar fallback for households registered before the first session — 'no session on record' is zero, which is what it has always meant.
